title: STRANGE MINUTE #20 · WHAT IF

lines.text: What if you ate 3,000 calories tonight?
lines.say: What if you ate three thousand calories tonight?

lines.text: That's a Thanksgiving dinner: more than a whole day of food, in one meal.
Your stomach stretches like a balloon to make room.
Extra blood rushes to your gut to digest it all.
Then comes the famous food coma.
Most people blame the turkey's tryptophan.
But turkey has about as much as chicken or cheese.
The real reason? All those carbs, and the sheer size of the meal.
Your insulin spikes, and you crash on the couch.
To burn it all off, you'd walk roughly 30 miles.
lines.say: To burn it all off, you'd walk roughly thirty miles.

lines.text: So, are you still going back for seconds?

youtube.title: What If You Ate A 3,000-Calorie Thanksgiving Dinner? 🦃😳 #shorts

youtube.first_comment: Happy Thanksgiving 🦃 Be honest — how many plates did YOU have? 👇

sources: Calorie Control Council (industry group) cited for ~3,000 (up to 4,500) calories on Thanksgiving; UGA extension: typical holiday meal 2,000–3,000
LiveScience / AIP Inside Science / Texas Health: turkey's tryptophan is similar to chicken, cheese, nuts; drowsiness comes from large carb-heavy meals, insulin, volume, alcohol
Walking burns roughly 80–120 kcal per mile → ~30 miles for 3,000 kcal (rough estimate)
After a meal, blood flow to the gut increases (postprandial splanchnic hyperemia)
